issues.description: generate-stories requires an existing stories manifest, so it cannot bootstrap the missing dataset described by the README.
Extraction requires pre-existing story files, but data/stories is empty, so the advertised demo path fails from a fresh checkout.
Model loading uses the newer dtype kwarg while pyproject allows transformers>=4.42, where torch_dtype is the compatible argument.
Core scientific dependencies are only lower-bounded, making runs and generated research artifacts non-reproducible across installs.
A one-token or effectively empty input can divide by zero when computing activation averaging weights.
PCA variance ratios divide by zero for zero-variance inputs, producing NaNs instead of a safe empty or validated result.
Bradley-Terry fitting uses unstable gradient descent and unclipped p_hat logs, which can overflow or produce infinite loss on extreme logits.
Neutral activation extraction materializes every token, layer, and hidden dimension in RAM, creating avoidable OOM risk as scale grows.
span_mean_activations silently returns zero vectors when spans match no tokens, which can corrupt downstream correlations without warning.
Story generation has no HTTP timeout, retry strategy, or atomic write behavior, so a network hang or partial failure can leave inconsistent data.
Ignored generated artifacts are nevertheless present in the tree, including emovec.egg-info and outputs.
Checked-in output artifacts claim an 80-story run, but the corresponding input dataset is not present, making the artifacts unauditable.
Dataset coverage is skipped when stories are absent, so the default test suite does not catch the broken fresh-checkout demo path.
Configuration values are cast but not validated, allowing invalid fractions, batch sizes, or PCA targets to fail later with unclear errors.
Steered-emotion selection does not guard against k exceeding available emotions, which can duplicate choices on smaller configs.
